newsitem.title: USA: Reynolds research papers key in Fla. case.
newsitem.headline: Reynolds research papers key in Fla. case.

text.p: A 1962 report by a top R.J. Reynolds Tobacco Co scientist, who advised the company cigarettes had caused harm to lab animals, will be key evidence in a late cancer victim's suit against the cigarette company, the plaintiff's attorney told jurors Wednesday.

Ron Motley, an attorney for the estate of Jean Connor, waved the documents in front of the jury and said they would prove Reynolds knew cigarette smoking injured animals in lab tests, but failed to share the evidence with the U.S. Surgeon General or the smoking public.

Reynolds is a unit of RJR Nabisco Holdings Corp. Motley also showed the jury a box of SnackWells chocolate cookies, which are made by Nabisco. He pointed out the label listing the cookie ingredients and said the company failed to make similar ingredient disclosures to smokers.
"Now R.J. Reynolds is a drug company and I'm going to prove it to you...They sell a drug called nicotine and they sell it in cigarettes," Motley said.
Conner filed a product liability suit against the tobacco company before her death from lung cancer in 1995. Her sister, Dana Raulerson, later sued the tobacco company on behalf of Connor's estate.

Motley told jurors he would reveal the "Secrets of Salem," the brand Connor smoked. During opening statements in the Jacksonville courtroom, he dramatically punctuated his comments by waving a Salem cigarette.
